extracted.intended_audience: Indian English-speaking news readers interested in politics, entertainment, and social commentary
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit criteria around writing/performing political stand-up comedy in an Indian context — what themes comics pick, how the public and authorities may react, and tonal choices to manage backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting socio-political contradictions ('Two Indias')
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate the 'Two Indias' — inner contradictions of India's socio-political landscape — as the core premise of the sketch or monologue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use juxtaposition to expose hypocrisy and conflicting social realities; the article gives examples respondents offered (e.g., northeast being called 'seven sisters' yet alienated from development; women judged for crop tops but a blouse considered 'sanskari'). Treat such contradictions as central beats of the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate legal and political backlash ('derogatory statements against India')
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that pointed commentary may provoke formal complaints or accusations (the piece notes two police complaints accusing Vir Das of making 'derogatory statements against India').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comics should understand potential legal risk and political consequences when addressing sensitive national topics; consider legal language, avoid unnecessarily defamatory factual claims, and plan responses to formal complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand unequal enforcement of expressive norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that different performers or public figures may be treated unequally — e.g., 'an actress who insults the freedom struggle simply "gets away" but a comedian doesn't even enjoy the basic freedom of cracking a joke.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing material, be mindful that comedians may be more exposed to penalties or targeted for criticism compared with other artists; framing, venue, and audience can affect tolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic selection: focus on hypocrisy, opportunism, and marginalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose themes that are resonant examples of 'Two Indias' — electoral opportunism, caste and temple access issues, regional neglect, gender double standards, and the co-opting/mocking of constitutional ideals like secularism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article's respondent-completions illustrate fertile subject-matter for political satire (e.g., 'Hindu before elections' vs being denied temple entry after polls; 'sickular' as mockery of secular defenders). Use specific, lived examples to make contrasts sharp and relatable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone management: balance critique with conciliatory sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider tonal choices that temper critique — Vir Das asked the audience 'to focus on the light, remember our greatness, and spread the love.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tackling sensitive national themes, some performers may choose to pair criticism with affirmations of shared values or hopeful language to reduce alienation and signal constructive intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect and plan for social media backlash and trolling
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare for mockery, trolling, and targeted ridicule (the article notes people protecting secularism are 'mocked and trolled as "sickular"').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate online amplification and hostile responses; have communication strategies, allies, and platforms to contextualize the work and respond to misrepresentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity and accuracy in public-facing presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain factual and presentational accuracy in published materials (the piece issues an editorial correction: 'Yash Marwah is from Let India Breathe. The video erroneously states it as Let Me Breathe. The error is regretted.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small factual errors in credits or claims can undercut credibility; verify names, organizations, and quotations before release.
